status: Research prototype — exploratory findings only. Not peer reviewed.
headline: Short-window ECOSTRESS signals show inter-annual variability in SNP April–June phenology, with a directional low in 2021 and recovery signal through 2023. 2024–2025 coverage is insufficient for seasonal characterization.

findings.summary: NDVI area means range from 0.109 (2021) to 0.163 (2023). The 2021 minimum is directionally consistent with documented drought conditions but requires independent field validation.
caveats: April–June window only — not full growing season
Area mean includes ~63% no-data pixels (bare rock, snow, persistent cloud)

findings.summary: ET area means show notable variability (1.167–2.147 mm/day for high-confidence years). 2020 and 2021 show the lowest values. 2024 (2.255 mm/day) is LOW CONFIDENCE with only 2 overpasses and should not be interpreted.
caveats: 2024 ET based on 2 overpasses only — analytically insufficient
April–June is early-season — peak ET typically occurs later in summer
findings.language_required: cautious — do not extrapolate 2024 ET value

findings.summary: ESI values range narrowly from 0.781 to 0.860 for high-confidence years, all in the moderate-to-high range (no extreme stress). The lowest ESI in 2023 (0.781) is unexpected given high NDVI — directional complexity not fully explained. 2024 (0.925) is LOW CONFIDENCE.
caveats: ESI is ET/PET ratio — higher PET in warmer years can lower ESI even with adequate actual ET
findings.language_required: directional — do not claim confirmed stress or recovery

hypotheses: The SNP April–June satellite signal shows inter-annual variability characteristic of alpine phenology.
The 2021 NDVI minimum (0.109) may reflect early-season drought. Directional signal only — requires ground-truth validation.
The NDVI recovery from 2021 to 2023 is a directional signal consistent with return to baseline, not a confirmed trend.
ESI values in the moderate range (0.78–0.86) across most years suggest the April–June period is not characterized by extreme stress conditions — but this window precedes peak-summer stress potential.
what_we_cannot_claim: Confirmed long-term vegetation trend (positive or negative)
Confirmed drought impact in 2021 from satellite data alone
2024 seasonal characterization for ET or ESI
Full growing season (July–September) conditions — analysis window ends in June
Sub-pixel spatial patterns — 70m resolution limits fine-scale inference
next_steps: Extend to full growing season (July–September) to capture peak phenology
Cross-validate with SNP ground-station records and phenology cameras
Increase 2024–2025 data density as additional overpasses are acquired
Formal trend analysis requires ≥10 years of data for statistical reliability
